rule: Two releases may only be compared area-by-area when the areas are established
to be the same ground. A shared GEOID is not evidence of that: identifiers are
reused across vintages even when the boundary moves.
When both releases use the same boundary vintage, equivalence holds by
construction and no further evidence is needed.
When the vintages differ, equivalence must be established one of two ways:
(a) computed geometry evidence: every area shared by the two releases is
compared polygon-to-polygon from the two cached boundary files, and every
one of them falls inside the tolerances below; or
(b) a reviewed equivalence record listed under reviewed_equivalences, naming
both vintages, the geography level, the evidence consulted, the reviewer
Neither branch treats a difference as demographic change, and neither treats an
equal identifier as a stable area. A difference inside the tolerances is
recorded as a cartographic generalisation difference and reported, not hidden.
A difference outside them blocks the comparison until a human reviews it and
either adds a record here or supplies a validated harmonisation.

note: A tenth of a percent of area and 25 metres of centroid movement are well
inside the redrawing the Census Bureau applies between annual 1:500,000
cartographic releases of an unchanged area, and far below any boundary
revision that would move population between areas. They are a starting
point chosen for this project, not a Census Bureau standard.
